text: . NOTE. Distinguish from Wild Thyme, p.2415. Pharmacopoeias. In Eur. (see p.vii). Ph. Eur. 6.2 (Thyme). The whole leaves and flowers separated from the previously dried stems of Thymus vulgaris, or T. zygis, or a mixture of both species. It contains not less than 12 mL/kg of essential oil, of which a minimum of 40% is thymol and car- vacrol, both calculated with reference to the anhydrous drug. It has a strong aromatic odour reminiscent of thymol. Profile Thyme is the source of thyme oil (below). It has carminative, antiseptic, antitussive, and expectorant properties and is used chiefly in preparations for respiratory-tract disorders and as a fla- vour.
